newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha edges up, holidays cloud prompt deals.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha edges up, holidays cloud prompt deals.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices edged higher on the back of Tuesday's late crude oil rally, but a round of European holidays clouded prompt deals and the timing of potential loadings, traders said on Wednesday.
May swaps rose $1 to about $182/$183 a tonne with June at $184/$185 and July at $184.50/$185.50, they said.
NWE cargoes were notionally valued at $180/$182 cif, up $2, but some brokers felt this was a bit rich.

One trader said he was bidding for 25-30,000 tonnes at $181 cif. He said at least one trader was offering material, but the prospect of one to two prompt cargoes on the market with several holidays in the next few days was making it difficult to work out timing details.
"The point is if you have a cargo ahead of the holiday and you expect people to jump up and down for it, that is not the way the market works," the trader said.
A broker said the NWE market otherwise was very slow on Wednesday and supply and demand relatively balanced.
"The market is balanced," he said. "End-users are not aggressively bidding on material...and the market is still reasonably supplied with supplies out of the U.K. and Russia."

Last week's fears over double-stem cargoes of naphtha being suspended at Skikda were unfounded, the trader said, adding the only limitations were due to congestion and poor weather at the Algerian port.
He said he was currently loading a double-stem cargo there.

Sonatrach has not been available to comment since last week when traders who had spoken to the company told Reuters that one of its jetties that handles large cargoes would be loading fuel oil only through this week.
